artifacts.description: feat(kernel): tapped hole cut at the metric coarse tap-drill diameter

acceptance_criteria: New documented variant `HoleKind::Tapped { thread: MetricThread }`. `MetricThread` derives `Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq` if it doesn't already. The doc comment says the cut is the tap-drill diameter (`MetricThread::tap_drill_diameter`) and that the thread is not modeled.

`OcctKernel::hole` cuts it for `Blind` and `ThroughAll`. The result equals `HoleKind::Simple { diameter: thread.tap_drill_diameter() }` with the same `at` and `depth`: same volume within 1e-9 relative, same face count. The existing `Simple`, `Counterbore` and `Countersink` tests still pass unchanged.

Tests (behind `occt`). Box `make_box((0, 0, 0), (40, 30, 20))`. Volumes within 1e-6 relative, boxes within 1e-6: M6 (tap drill Ø5), through all at (20, 15, 20) along −Z: volume 24000 − 125π ≈ 23607.3009; 7 faces; bounding box unchanged. M6, blind 10, same axis: volume 24000 − 62.5π ≈ 23803.6505; 8 faces; the hole bottom face's box is (17.5, 12.5, 10)–(22.5, 17.5, 10). `metric_coarse("M10")` (tap drill Ø8.5), through all, same axis: volume ≈ 22865.0997. The input solid is unchanged (volume 24000, 6 faces).

Errors, each with a test and never a panic, all `InvalidInput` and checked before the backend, with kernel-free tests without `occt` in `hole.rs`: a hand-built `MetricThread` whose `nominal` or `pitch` is zero, negative or not finite, or whose `pitch` ≥ `nominal`.
No new dependencies, no new `unsafe`, and `swx-kernel` still has no workspace dependencies.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and so do the CI `swx-kernel (occt)` job commands.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
